feedback.problem:
Consider the set $A,$ defined as

$$
A={{n}^{4}:n\in Z}.
$$

Which of the following sets is equivalent to $A?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The elements of $A$ are all the terms of the sequence ${a}_{n},$ given by

$$
{a}_{n}={n}^{4},\,n\in Z={0,\pm 1,\pm 2,\pm 3,…}.
$$

Let's write down some terms of our sequence until the pattern becomes clear.

$$
\begin{aligned} & ⋮ \\ {a}_{-3} & =(-3)^{4}=81 \\ {a}_{-2} & =(-2)^{4}=16 \\ {a}_{-1} & =(-1)^{4}=1 \\ {a}_{0} & ={0}^{4}=0 \\ {a}_{1} & ={1}^{4}=1 \\ {a}_{2} & ={2}^{4}=16 \\ {a}_{3} & ={3}^{4}=81 \\  & ⋮\end{aligned}
$$

So, the set consists of the elements

$$
A={0,1,16,81…}.
$$

These are just the fourth powers including $0.$ Continuing the pattern, we have

$$
A={0,1,16,81,256,625,…}.
$$
